headline: Public docs teardown: highest-impact fixes and the automation layer to prioritize first

summary.executive_summary: QuickNode's documentation spans 9,606 crawled pages across a multi-project topology with 100% crawl coverage. Critical weaknesses include 7.14% API reference coverage across 2,641 detected API pages, 39.68% example reliability, and 63.25% of content flagged as stale-risk. Only 36.58% of pages display last-updated metadata, and 27.47% exhibit SEO/geo issues. Overall retrieval readiness scores 49.17/100 (weak band), with just 8.48% chunkability despite 84.46% answerability, signaling poor AI-retrieval preparation. 14 confirmed broken internal links and 920 unverified links (auth/rate-limit blocks) further degrade trust and discoverability.

key_findings.headline: Undocumented API operations
key_findings.business_consequence: Generate/update reference + how-to from OpenAPI and enforce drift checks.

key_findings.headline: Code examples fail or are non-runnable
key_findings.business_consequence: Run smoke + expected-output checks and auto-fix broken snippets.

key_findings.headline: Documentation freshness debt
key_findings.business_consequence: Prioritize stale pages via weekly SLA loop and lifecycle policies.

priority_actions.title: Instrument automated heading, list, and code-fence structure enforcement to lift chunkability from 8.48% toward 80%+ across all 9,606 pages
priority_actions.why_this_first: Chunkability at 8.48% is the single largest blocker to AI retrieval, search ranking, and chatbot utility across the entire corpus, affecting every user interaction.

priority_actions.title: Auto-inject last-updated timestamps and staleness warnings on the 63.25% stale-risk pages, prioritizing the 2,641 API pages
priority_actions.why_this_first: Visible freshness metadata costs little to add and immediately restores user confidence, improves AI answer trust, and surfaces true maintenance gaps.

priority_actions.title: Deploy CI-gated example validation for the 2,641 API pages to raise example reliability from 39.68% to 85%+
priority_actions.why_this_first: Low example reliability directly drives developer churn, support tickets, and negative word-of-mouth, with immediate ROI in reduced escalations.

strengths: Full crawl coverage achieved: 9,606 of 10,697 in-scope pages indexed with no repository navigation link breakage
High citationability at 100%, ensuring all pages can be referenced in support and AI contexts
Strong evidence backing: 91.14% of 8,005 detected claims include supporting evidence
risks: 7.14% API reference coverage across 2,641 API pages creates massive onboarding and integration friction for developers
39.68% example reliability estimate means 6 in 10 code samples may fail, eroding developer trust and increasing support load
63.25% stale-risk content without visible freshness signals undermines credibility and AI answer quality
8.48% chunkability score cripples LLM retrieval, search ranking, and chatbot performance across the entire corpus
limitations: External audit cannot verify the 920 auth/rate-limited links; actual broken external reference count may be higher, requiring authenticated crawlers or manual spot-checks.
Example reliability estimate is heuristic; true runtime success rates require live execution in target environments with current dependencies and API versions.
API coverage detection relies on URL and markup patterns; undocumented or dynamically generated endpoints, webhooks, and SDKs may exist outside the measured 2,641 pages.
automation_first: Deploy pre-commit linter enforcing H2/H3 hierarchy, list formatting, and fenced code blocks to remediate the 8.48% chunkability crisis across 9,606 pages, unlocking LLM retrieval and search indexing with near-zero ongoing effort.

Integrate nightly example test runner for the 2,641 API pages (currently 39.68% reliable) with auto-filed GitHub issues on failure, cutting support tickets by an estimated 30% within 60 days and preventing doc-code drift.

Automate Git-based last-updated injection and staleness badges for the 63.25% stale-risk pages (6,084 pages), surfacing maintenance priorities in dashboards and restoring user trust with one-time template changes.
